key_insight: Harness-Zero shows that instead of only using a strong external harness at deployment, you can use a domain- or instance-optimized harness during training to distill its benefits into the agent itself. This helps agents generalize better without depending on a perfect harness at test time.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the problem that agent performance often depends heavily on the external harness used to interact with the environment, and the best harness varies by domain, task instance, and model. This creates a deployment challenge: a shared harness may be suboptimal, while maintaining many specialized harnesses is complex and hard to scale.
method: Use a stronger, optimized harness as a training-time guide rather than a permanent deployment dependency.
Distill the behavior and advantages of specialized harnesses into the agent model so it can retain performance gains independently.
Reduce the need to route among multiple harnesses at inference time by transferring harness-specific improvements into the agent itself.
impact: For AI practitioners, this offers a practical path to building more robust agents that are less tied to brittle or expensive external tooling. It could simplify deployment while improving performance across diverse tasks and domains.
